title: Case Study: This Platform's RAG Pipeline Check

questions.questionText: How does this platform's content sync script chunk lesson content?
options: By a fixed character count, regardless of content structure
By heading — structure-aware chunking, so each chunk corresponds to one coherent section
It doesn't chunk content at all, each entire lesson is one chunk
questions.correctAnswer: By heading — structure-aware chunking, so each chunk corresponds to one coherent section
questions.explanation: This directly applies the chunking-strategies lesson's structure-aware approach: splitting at headings keeps each chunk a coherent unit rather than an arbitrary slice.

questions.questionText: Why does the platform store embeddings in pgvector within the same Postgres instance, rather than a separate dedicated vector database?
options: pgvector is the only vector storage option that exists
The corpus is curriculum-sized (low thousands of chunks), so one database keeps the system simpler than operating a second specialized store for what a modest ANN index can already handle
Dedicated vector databases cannot use HNSW indexes
It's required for the tutor to work at all
questions.correctAnswer: The corpus is curriculum-sized (low thousands of chunks), so one database keeps the system simpler than operating a second specialized store for what a modest ANN index can already handle
questions.explanation: At this scale, pgvector's HNSW index performs fine, and consolidating into one database avoids the operational overhead of a separate vector database for no real benefit.

questions.questionText: Why does the tutor scope retrieval to the current lesson/course instead of searching the entire curriculum for every question?
options: It doesn't — it always searches everything
It's a concrete application of selective retrieval / context engineering: narrowing the search space with known application context improves both precision and speed
Scoping is required by the embedding model itself
It has no effect on retrieval quality
questions.correctAnswer: It's a concrete application of selective retrieval / context engineering: narrowing the search space with known application context improves both precision and speed
questions.explanation: Using the fact that the user is reading a specific lesson to scope retrieval before even computing similarity is a direct, practical instance of the selective-retrieval context engineering technique.
